project.name: class-booking
project.what: Bookings and payments for small fitness studios: a Rust API and a React app

understanding.project: class-booking is a product for small fitness studios: a studio publishes its classes, and its clients book a place and pay by card. Most users are in Spain and Portugal, about 300 people a day at launch.
understanding.today: Nothing is built yet. The person has chosen Rust with Axum for the API and React for the pages, and expects about 20% more visitors a month in the first year.
understanding.plan: We will build one Cloud Run service for the API and the pages, keep bookings in Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL and class photos in Cloud Storage, and send reminders from a Cloud Run job that Cloud Scheduler starts every 15 minutes. Payment webhooks are checked and answered at once. Nothing runs while nobody uses the product, so the first months cost little.

prices.source: Google Cloud pricing pages, read 2026-10-09: Cloud Run Tier 1 and its free tiers, Cloud SQL db-f1-micro and SSD and Secret Manager as published; Tier 2 is Tier 1 x 1.4; Cloud SQL and Cloud Storage outside europe-west1 and us-central1 are estimates. Firestore Standard edition from the Cloud Billing Catalog, read 2026-10-13: reads, writes and storage at europe-west1's price in every region (the catalog lists $0.03 to $0.06 per 100,000 reads across these regions); its free quota of 50,000 reads, 20,000 writes and 1 GiB a day covers one database a project, is counted in operations, so it is the same in every region, and a month holds 30 days of it. Checked against Google's bill and pricing pages 2026-10-11: Cloud Storage keeps 5,000 free class A operations in every region (the 5 GB of storage is US-only); egress stays at the published $0.12 a GB although Cloud Run bills $0.105 a GiB from Europe to Europe. Twelve more regions added 2026-10-12: each region's Cloud Run tier from Google's Cloud Run locations page, read 2026-10-12; their Cloud SQL and Cloud Storage factors are estimates; the 5 GB free Cloud Storage applies in us-central1, us-east1 and us-west1

findings.title: Reminders run as a job on a schedule
findings.why: A timer inside the API would run on every copy at once, or on none when nobody calls.
findings.fix: Cloud Scheduler starts a Cloud Run job every 15 minutes; it sends what is due and exits.

findings.title: Payment webhooks answer at once; the work goes to a task
findings.why: A payment provider retries a webhook that answers late, and a copy may stop as soon as it has answered.
findings.fix: The handler checks the signature, queues a Cloud Task and answers 200; the task does the booking.

findings.title: Sessions in signed cookies
findings.code: a signed cookie store, the key in Secret Manager
findings.why: Copies come and go, so a session kept in one copy's memory is lost on the next request.
findings.fix: A signed, encrypted cookie holds the session; no Redis to pay for.

tasks.title: Infrastructure: service, Cloud SQL, bucket, scheduler
tasks.detail: Max 3 instances and a database pool of 5 a copy, because db-f1-micro takes 25 connections. This plan deploys from the repository with gcloud, so the project needs a billing account: the Starter Tier takes only apps published from Google AI Studio, and Cloud Scheduler, Cloud Storage are outside its four products. A person who never had a billing account starts on Google's Free Trial: $300 of credit for 90 days, nothing billed until they upgrade to a paid account (docs.cloud.google.com/free/docs/free-cloud-features). Creating or linking the account is the person's step: ask with `exodus need`.

tasks.title: Budget and alerts
tasks.detail: A Cloud Billing budget of $12 a month on this project (the Cloud Run estimate rounded up, at least $5), with email alerts to the billing admins at 50%, 90% and 100% of actual spend and at 100% of the forecast: `gcloud billing budgets create --billing-account=BILLING_ACCOUNT_ID --display-name="class-booking on Cloud Run" --budget-amount=12USD --calendar-period=month --filter-projects=projects/PROJECT_ID --threshold-rule=percent=0.5 --threshold-rule=percent=0.9 --threshold-rule=percent=1.0 --threshold-rule=percent=1.0,basis=forecasted-spend` (the currency is the billing account's own; `--notifications-rule-pubsub-topic` adds a Pub/Sub topic for automated reactions). It needs Billing Account Administrator or Billing Account Costs Manager, or the project's owner for a budget on this project only. It changes billing settings: the agent shows the command, the person approves, and it runs with the person's own gcloud. How budgets work: https://exodus.elim.io/blog/budget-alerts-and-the-billing-export. Then a spend cap of $24 a month, a second budget that stops Cloud Run instead of only warning: in the console, Billing, Budgets & alerts, Create new budget, Spend cap enforcement, this project, the service Cloud Run, the amount $24 (or the Cloud Billing Budget API: `spendCap.inputState` CONFIGURED, the service `services/152E-C115-5142`, `creditTypesTreatment` EXCLUDE_ALL_CREDITS, thresholds at 50%, 80% and 100%, the full request on Google's page below). Past the cap, Cloud Run in this project pauses until the 1st of the next month or until the person lifts the cap: services answer 5xx, jobs and worker pools stop, nothing is deleted. It counts gross list-price costs before savings and credits and fires before the bill shows them, so it sits at twice the budget, at least $10, not at the estimate. It is not instant: what runs before it fires is billed as usual. Spend caps are monthly, for one project and one service; alerts go to the billing admins and project owners at 50%, 80% and 100%. It needs `billing.budgets.configureSpendCap` on the billing account, or `billing.resourcebudgets.configureSpendCap` on the project. Turning the app off at a ceiling is the person's call: the agent explains it, shows the steps and waits for a yes or no. How spend caps work: https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/budgets-spend-caps.
